https://www.barrons.com/articles/dow-jumps-300-points-because-the-fed-is-listening-after-all-51545406538 Dow Jumps 300 Points Because the Fed Is Listening After All By Dec. 21, 2018 10:35 a.m. ET Order Reprints Michael Haddad Text size
10:27 a.m. The Dow Jones Industrial Average is soaring after Federal Reserve Bank of New York President John Williams said that being data dependent means listening to the markets too .
The S&P 500 has gained 1.3% to 2500.32, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average has climbed 356.29 points, or 1.6%, 23,215.89. The Nasdaq Composite has risen 0.8% to 6577.82.
The market tumbled the past two days after the Fed left the impression that it didn’t care what the market thought when it hiked rates by a quarter point on Wednesday , and issued forecasts that pointed to two more increases in 2019. It also left the impression that the so-called Fed put is dead. Williams comments suggest that it’s not. “He said ‘judges’ was a softer way of saying ‘expects’ and thus tempers the ‘gradual’ path they are on,” writes Peter Boockvar , chief investment officer at Bleakley Advisory Group . “Markets rallied right after.”
Still, the market’s reaction isn’t all good news. While we might expect tech and communications services to underperform—they’ve each gained 0.8% as investors look for new opportunities outside Apple (AAPL), Facebook (FB) and the other FAANGs—industrials are up 0.8%, suggesting that investors aren’t willing to stop betting on a slowdown yet. And the best performers? Utilities and materials, two sectors that benefit from lower interest rates.
It’s a mixed message, and we’d prefer something a little more straightforward before we get too excited.
